title: Edit formula

errors.nesting: This formula nests too many levels deep.
errors.method: A property or function should come next.
errors.pageMethod: A property or function should come next.
errors.nonBlockProperty: Properties can only be read from a page.
errors.typeOperation: Math doesn’t work between {{left}} and {{right}} values.
errors.typeUnary: {{type}} values can’t take a minus sign.
errors.resultType: A formula can’t return {{type}}. It may return {{name}} or undefined.
errors.argumentsMissing: {{name}}() is short of arguments: it needs {{expected}} and has {{given}}.
errors.roundNonInteger: Rounding needs a whole number of decimal places, not {{precision}}.
errors.roundTooManyPlaces: Rounding stops at 12 decimal places, so {{precision}} won’t work.
errors.toNumberList: A list can’t go into toNumber(); use first() or at() for one item, or map() for each.
errors.durationUnit: “{{unit}}” is not a time unit {{name}}() knows.
errors.unsafePattern: Regular expressions can’t repeat a group that already repeats, such as (a+)+.

operators.remainder: What is left after dividing the left number by the right.
operators.power: The left number to the power of the right.
operators.equal: Whether the two values are the same.
operators.greater: Whether the left value is greater than the right.
operators.greaterOrEqual: Whether the left value is at least the right.
operators.less: Whether the left value is less than the right.
operators.lessOrEqual: Whether the left value is at most the right.
operators.condition: The second value when the condition holds, else the third.
operators.not: Flips true to false and false to true.

functions.if: Checks the condition: true gives the first value, false the second.
functions.ifs: Checks the conditions in turn and gives the value that goes with the first true one. A shorter way to write if() inside if().
functions.let: Names a value, then works out the expression using that name.
functions.lets: Names several values, then works out the expression using those names.
functions.not: Flips true to false and false to true.
functions.empty: Whether the value is empty: 0, “”, false, [] and blank properties all count. With nothing inside the brackets, it gives an empty value.
functions.length: How many characters a text has, or how many items a list has.
functions.format: The value written out as text.
functions.equal: Whether the two values are the same.
functions.substring: Part of the text, from startIndex up to but not including endIndex; without endIndex, to the end.
functions.contains: Whether the search text appears in the value.
functions.startsWith: Whether a text starts with another.
functions.endsWith: Whether a text ends with another.
functions.test: Whether the text fits the pattern, a regular expression.
functions.match: A list of every part of the text that fits the pattern, a regular expression.
functions.replace: Swaps the first part that fits the pattern for the replacement.
functions.replaceAll: Swaps every part that fits the pattern for the replacement.
functions.trim: The text with spaces cut off both ends.
functions.repeat: The text repeated count times, end to end.
functions.padStart: Adds padString to the front of the text until it is targetLength long.
functions.padEnd: Adds padString to the end of the text until it is targetLength long.
functions.link: A link that shows the text and opens the url.
functions.style: Formats the text. Styles: “b” bold, “i” italic, “u” underline, “s” strikethrough, “c” code. Colors: “gray”, “brown”, “orange”, “yellow”, “green”, “blue”, “purple”, “pink”, “red”; add “_background” to a color for a background instead.
functions.unstyle: Takes formatting off the text: the styles named, or all of it when none are named.
functions.split: Cuts the text at each separator and gives the pieces as a list.
functions.join: Puts the list’s items together into one text, with the joiner between them.
functions.formatNumber:
The number written as text.

format is “commas” (the default), “percent”, “humanize”, “bytes_binary”, “bytes_decimal” or one of the currency codes below.

precision sets how many decimal places show, from 0 to 12.

Currency codes: “usd”, “aud”, “cad”, “sgd”, “eur”, “gbp”, “jpy”, “rub”, “inr”, “krw”, “cny”, “brl”, “try”, “idr”, “chf”, “hkd”, “nzd”, “sek”, “nok”, “mxn”, “zar”, “twd”, “dkk”, “pln”, “thb”, “huf”, “czk”, “ils”, “clp”, “php”, “aed”, “cop”, “sar”, “myr”, “ron”, “ars”, “uyu”, “pen”, “vnd”, “pkr”, “ngn”.
functions.toNumber: Turns text, or another value, into a number.
functions.subtract: The second number taken away from the first.
functions.divide: The first number divided by the second.
functions.mod: What is left after dividing the first number by the second.
functions.pow: The first number to the power of the second.
functions.min: The smallest of the numbers given.
functions.max: The largest of the numbers given.
functions.sum: All the numbers given, added up.
functions.mean: The average of the numbers given.
functions.median: The middle one of the numbers given, once they are in order.
functions.abs: The number without its sign: a negative number becomes positive.
functions.round: The number rounded to the nearest whole number.
functions.ceil: The number rounded up to a whole number.
functions.floor: The number rounded down to a whole number.
functions.sqrt: The number’s square root, the positive one.
functions.exp: e (about 2.718, the base of the natural log) to the power of the number.
functions.ln: The number’s natural log, in base e.
functions.sign: 1 for a positive number, -1 for a negative one, 0 for zero.
functions.pi: π, a circle’s circumference over its diameter (about 3.14159).
functions.e: e, the base of the natural log (about 2.71828).
functions.now: The date and time right now.
functions.today: Today’s date, with no time of day.
functions.parseDate: Reads a date written in ISO 8601 form, such as 2022-01-01.
functions.nextWorkday: The date if it is a working day, else the next one: no weekend day or public holiday (Korea’s, or a calendar’s code).
functions.addWorkdays: A date moved by a count of working days, skipping weekends and public holidays (Korea’s, or a calendar’s code).
functions.formatDate: Writes the date as text in the format given, and in another time zone if one is named. In the format, “YYYY” is the year, “MM” the month, “DD” the day, “HH” the hour and “mm” the minute.
functions.dateAdd: The date with num units added. unit is one of “years”, “quarters”, “months”, “weeks”, “days”, “hours” and “minutes”.
functions.dateSubtract: The date with num units taken away. unit is one of “years”, “quarters”, “months”, “weeks”, “days”, “hours” and “minutes”.
functions.dateBetween: The first date minus the second, counted in unit: one of “years”, “quarters”, “months”, “weeks”, “days”, “hours” and “minutes”.
functions.dateRange: A date range that runs from the start date to the end date.
functions.dateStart: The first date of a date range.
functions.dateEnd: The last date of a date range.
functions.timestamp: The date as a Unix timestamp: the milliseconds since January 1, 1970.
functions.fromTimestamp: The date a Unix timestamp stands for (milliseconds since January 1, 1970), without its seconds and milliseconds.
functions.week: The date’s ISO week of the year, from 1 to 53.
functions.date: The date’s day of the month, from 1 to 31.
functions.day: The date’s weekday as a number, from 1 for Monday to 7 for Sunday.
functions.at: The list item at position index, counting from 0.
functions.slice: Part of the list, from startIndex up to but not including endIndex; without endIndex, to the end.
functions.concat: The lists joined end to end into one list.
functions.sort: The list put in order. Give an expression to choose what each item is sorted by.
functions.unique: The list with repeated values left out.
functions.includes: Whether the list holds the search value.
functions.find: The first item in the list that meets the condition.
functions.findIndex: Where the first item meeting the condition sits in the list, counting from 0.
functions.filter: Only the items in the list that meet the condition.
functions.some: Whether at least one item in the list meets the condition.
functions.every: Whether every item in the list meets the condition.
functions.map: A new list made by working out the expression for each item.
functions.flat: Takes the items out of nested lists and puts them in one list.
functions.name: The person’s name.
functions.id: The ID of a page or person. Left empty, it is the ID of the page this formula is on.
functions.splice: Takes deleteCount items out of the list at startIndex, then puts any further values in their place. Without deleteCount, nothing is taken out.
functions.count: How many items in the list meet the condition. Without a condition, every item counts, as length() does.

emptyValueCall: This call may be given an empty value.
unknownTargetCall: {{name}}() is used on a value that might not be of type {{type}}.
unknownArgumentCall: {{name}}() is given a value that might not be of type {{type}}.
